decoded.meaning: SPEC{NAME "name" NAME "up", NAME "config" SETTINGS{NAME "addr" NAME "127.0.0.1", NAME "port" VALUE u16=8080}} — RFC-0014 §2 `create-via-SPEC`, the payload written to /net/<module>/conn
decoded.note: The creator-endpoint spelling carries `{ name, config }` and NOTHING else. No `type`: the module segment in the path already selects the transport, so there is no catalog type to name. No `role`: RFC-0014 §1/§3 make the role POSITIONAL — the module the endpoint belongs to is `DIAL` or `LISTEN`, and a `role` pair in this config is an unknown pair, ignored rather than obeyed. The superseded global `:children[]` spelling, which had to carry both, was retired with its door by RFC-0014 Amendment 4 (S7). The config also carries the mixed-value-type claim the retired `spec/conn-client-ws` vector used to hold: `addr` is a textual NAME, `port` an opaque VALUE u16, and neither form substitutes for the other. Bytes emitted by tr::net::conn_spec_t's (endpoint) constructor.
